clue.text: Reportedly purchase something old in Egypt, a form of crystal

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so the word for purchase is heard

parts.note: to purchase is to buy
the pyramids are ancient Egyptian monuments

explanation.surface: A tourist told of buying an antiquity in Egypt, a sort of crystal.
explanation.walkthrough: BUY said out loud gives the prefix BI.
explanation.definitionFit: A bipyramid is a crystal shape made of two pyramids joined base to base.

clue.text: There's no art in one's party game

parts.note: one is I, so one's is I plus S

indicators.note: there's no art in party means the letters a-r-t are taken out of it

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A remark that one's party game needs no artistic talent.
explanation.walkthrough: PARTY with ART taken out leaves PY, after I'S.
explanation.definitionFit: I spy is the children's guessing game of spotting things by their first letter.

clue.text: Man implicated in divorce

indicators.note: implicated in suggests caught up inside, so the name lies within the word

explanation.surface: A man named in divorce proceedings.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivor is a man's first name.

clue.text: Flock to English spouse, an offal retailer

parts.note: a trip is a small flock of sheep or goats
a wife is a spouse

explanation.surface: A flock goes to an Englishman's wife, who sells offal.
explanation.definitionFit: A tripewife is a woman who sells tripe and other innards.

clue.text: Steak giving disease to single person

parts.note: TB is the usual short form of tuberculosis
one person, a lone individual, is ONE

explanation.surface: A butcher's cut said to infect someone living alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A T-shaped bone runs through this cut of beef, a classic grilling steak.

clue.text: Cut off the edge

parts.note: read plainly, to clip away the margin, as one does to a hedge or hair

explanation.definitionFit: To trim is to neaten something by clipping its margins.

clue.text: Criminals group together to get the thing sought up and down

parts.note: to band is to group together
it is the thing sought, as in the game of tag

indicators.note: in a down clue up means reversed, so the same word reads one way then back

parts.note: it is the thing sought, as in the game of tag

explanation.surface: Gangsters unite to get what they are after.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up and down' gives IT twice, once forwards and once backwards (TI).
explanation.definitionFit: Banditti is the Italian plural for outlaws or brigands.

clue.text: To do too much retail therapy is non-U and a little bit off

indicators.note: non-U here means without U, so that letter is dropped

parts.words: To do too much retail therapy
parts.note: retail therapy is shopping, so doing too much is buying too much

explanation.surface: Shopping too much is common and slightly off.
explanation.walkthrough: Non-U normally means not upper-class; here it means remove U. Overby is a Scots word for a little way off.
explanation.definitionFit: Overby means near at hand, just across the way.

clue.text: On Tuesday earns — the next working day after this?

definitions.text: On Tuesday earns — the next working day after this?

indicators.note: working means set in motion, so the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone paid on Tuesday wonders which holiday came before.
explanation.walkthrough: Easter Monday is a bank holiday in Britain, so the next working day after this Sunday is Tuesday.
explanation.definitionFit: The day of the Resurrection festival is followed in Britain by a Monday holiday, so Tuesday is the next workday.

clue.text: As good as a mile, one's found, in motorways

indicators.note: the clue's 'found, in' places the first piece inside the second

parts.note: M is a motorway, so two of them are MS
one is I, so 'one's' gives I plus S

explanation.surface: A driver musing on distances among the motorway network.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition completes the proverb 'a miss is as good as a mile'.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says a narrow failure counts the same as a wide one.

clue.text: Priest has Bible publicity rejected in red-top newspaper?

parts.note: AV is the Authorised Version of the Bible

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the word for publicity is read backwards

parts.note: an ad is publicity, an advertisement

explanation.surface: A clergyman's scripture advertisement turned down by a tabloid.
explanation.walkthrough: Red-top normally means a British tabloid such as the Sun; here 'red' means communist, and this was the Soviet Party's top paper.
explanation.definitionFit: It was the official daily of the Soviet Communist Party, a newspaper of the Reds.

clue.text: One thing to catch fish is surrounded by others of these materials

indicators.note: the second piece is enclosed by the first, as the clue says

parts.note: toils are nets or snares, so more things to catch fish
one is the Roman numeral I
a net catches fish

explanation.surface: A fisherman's net hemmed in by more nets.
explanation.walkthrough: TOILS (nets, snares) wraps I + NET. Toilinet is a fine fabric of silk or cotton warp and woollen weft.
explanation.definitionFit: Toilinets are fabrics used for waistcoats, so they are cloth materials.

clue.text: To absorb DIY yardsticks needs a month

indicators.note: to absorb is to take inside, so the letters are held within the clue's words

explanation.surface: Home-improvement rulers need a month to soak in.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'DIY yardsticks'. Iyyar is the eighth month of the Jewish calendar.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the eighth month of the Jewish year, falling around April to May.

clue.text: Man could display this, one so volatile about nothing

clue.text: Everything and nothing to chart in ghost-writing?

parts.note: everything is all
nothing is zero, the letter O
a graph is a chart

explanation.surface: A ghost-writer charting everything and nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: An allograph is writing made by one person on another's behalf, as a ghost-writer does.

clue.text: Concerning endless libel peddled by papers — they should be this

parts.note: re means concerning or about
the papers, newspapers collectively, are the press

indicators.note: peddled suggests goods being hawked about, so these letters are moved around
endless means the final letter of libel is cut off

explanation.surface: Defamation spread by newspapers suggests they ought to be curbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' takes the last L off LIBEL to leave LIBE, which 'peddled' rearranges as IBLE. 'by' puts PRESS beside RE. The definition reads back to 'papers': they should be capable of being held in check.
explanation.definitionFit: A capable-of-being-held-down quality is what the clue says newspapers ought to have.

clue.text: Maybe she tucked into bodily sustenance and spiritual sustenance

indicators.note: tucked into means put inside the bread

parts.note: pitta is a flat bread, food for the body

indicators.note: maybe says the letters of she are a possible arrangement

explanation.surface: A woman eating bread and taking in religion too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' rearranges SHE as ESH, put inside PITTA. The Peshitta is the Syriac Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: The Peshitta is the standard Syriac Bible, nourishment for the soul.

clue.text: Transport over trowel to move plant

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word for transport is read backwards

parts.note: a van is a vehicle, a means of transport

indicators.note: to move tells us to shift the letters of trowel about

explanation.surface: Gardening instructions: take the trowel and move a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns VAN into NAV; 'to move' rearranges TROWEL into ELWORT.
explanation.definitionFit: Navelwort is pennywort, a wall plant with round fleshy leaves dimpled at the centre.

clue.text: Marsh's trees

explanation.surface: A crime writer's trees.
explanation.walkthrough: Ngaio Marsh was a New Zealand crime novelist; read with the apostrophe, the word is her first name in the possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Ngaio was the novelist's first name, and ngaios are New Zealand evergreen trees.

clue.text: Street toilets vandalised could these have been used?

indicators.note: vandalised means smashed up, so these letters are wrecked and rearranged

explanation.surface: Investigators wonder what tools damaged the public lavatories.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition looks back at the vandalism: narrow daggers could have done the damage.
explanation.definitionFit: Small slim daggers are the weapons a vandal might have used.

clue.text: Like a fox, as taxi driver in the early hours?

definitions.text: as taxi driver in the early hours?

explanation.surface: A cunning cabbie working the night shift.
explanation.walkthrough: The fox roams after dark; the second definition reads as a taxi driver carrying fares at night.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means travelling by night, which suits both a prowling fox and a cabbie taking night fares.

clue.text: Friendly island to spend time in

indicators.note: in places the short time inside the island

parts.note: May is an island in the Firth of Forth, Scotland

explanation.surface: A sociable isle where you spend time.
explanation.definitionFit: Maty means chummy and sociable.

clue.text: Old star found in cluster normally

indicators.note: found in says the letters sit inside the clue's words

explanation.surface: An astronomer's note that an ancient sun usually lies within a cluster.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'cluster normally'. Stern is an old and Scots word for a star.
explanation.definitionFit: Stern is an archaic word for a heavenly body that shines.

clue.text: Boiled a drink for use with whisky?

parts.note: sod is an old past tense of seethe, to boil

explanation.surface: Boiling a drink for whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: Soda water is the classic mixer for whisky.

clue.text: Held up highly glazed finish? Fine

indicators.note: held up in a down clue means read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: cire is a highly glazed finish on fabric

explanation.surface: A glossy finish is delayed, but that is fine.
explanation.walkthrough: An eric was a fine paid in old Irish law for a killing.
explanation.definitionFit: Eric was the blood-money penalty paid under Irish Brehon law.

clue.text: Sincerest flattery maybe could make you aim into it

indicators.note: could make suggests building something new out of these letters

explanation.surface: A coach tells you to aim at copying someone admiringly.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb runs: copying is the sincerest form of flattery; 'maybe' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying calls copying someone the sincerest way to flatter them.

clue.text: Terrier finds place to sleep in a filthy place

indicators.note: in places the bed inside the dirty pen

parts.note: a sty is a pigpen, a byword for filth
a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: A dog finds a bed in a dirty pen.
explanation.definitionFit: Scotty is the pet name for the Scottish terrier breed of dog.

clue.text: Kiss one for money in Croatia

parts.note: to lip is to kiss, touch with the lips
one is A, the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A traveller paying for a kiss in Croatia.
explanation.definitionFit: The lipa was the hundredth part of the kuna, Croatia's coin before the euro.

clue.text: Try to bring back old Palestinian leader? That's not right

indicators.note: not right says R, the abbreviation for right, is dropped
to bring back means the name is reversed, brought back the other way

parts.note: Yasser Arafat led the Palestine Liberation Organisation

explanation.surface: An attempt to revive a former Palestinian leader is condemned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to bring back' turns YASSER into RESSAY; 'That's not right' removes the R, leaving the word for an attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: An essay is an attempt, so to essay is to have a go.

clue.text: It's irregular, of course, in Seychelles

indicators.note: in puts the slang word inside the country code

parts.note: SY is the international vehicle code for Seychelles
natch is slang for naturally, of course

explanation.surface: An observation that something unusual naturally happens in the Seychelles.
explanation.walkthrough: Snatchy means coming in snatches, fitful.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done in snatches is fitful, jerky and uneven.
